evidence.claim: Investment was weak and domestic policy uncertainty increased, especially after proposals to reform the electricity market; the OECD urged certainty about existing contracts and regulatory stability.
evidence.title: Key Policy Insights: OECD Economic Surveys: Mexico 2022
evidence.excerpt: Investment was weak and domestic policy uncertainty increased, especially after proposals to reform the electricity market; the OECD urged certainty about existing contracts and regulatory stability.
evidence.source_locator: section on restarting investment and boosting productivity
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent policy analysis with explicit causation and clear relevance to ruler-period policy choices.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to 2022 policy settings and investor expectations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to AMLO because the uncertainty arose from his government’s energy-policy proposals and regulatory direction.
contrary_evidence: The OECD also says Mexico could benefit from U.S. recovery and nearshoring, so the environment was not uniformly adverse.
Investment weakness predates 2022, so this is partly inherited.

evidence.claim: Mexico’s anti-inflation subsidies cost about 575 billion pesos in 2022, including 430 billion pesos for gasoline subsidies, 73 billion for domestic energy subsidies, and 69 billion for food-security measures.
evidence.title: Mexico anti-inflation subsidies come with $28 billion price tag
evidence.excerpt: Mexico’s anti-inflation subsidies cost about 575 billion pesos in 2022, including 430 billion pesos for gasoline subsidies, 73 billion for domestic energy subsidies, and 69 billion for food-security measures.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters story text / government figures cited in article
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters cites government figures and provides clear policy composition and fiscal scale.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 policy response to inflation during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the AMLO government because officials announced and defended the measures alongside the president.
contrary_evidence: The measures were large and partly untargeted, so they may have been blunt rather than efficient.
The fiscal cost was high even if the policy eased consumer pain.

evidence.claim: The 2022 federal budget was presented as guaranteeing continuity for welfare programs, pensions, scholarships, producer support, and strategic infrastructure works such as Tren Maya, Dos Bocas, and the AIFA.
evidence.title: PEF 2022 garantiza continuidad de programas sociales y obras de desarrollo
evidence.publisher: Presidencia de la República 2018-2024 | Gobierno | gob.mx
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 federal budget was presented as guaranteeing continuity for welfare programs, pensions, scholarships, producer support, and strategic infrastructure works such as Tren Maya, Dos Bocas, and the AIFA.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget-policy statement from the presidency with concrete spending priorities.
evidence.period_fit: Budget for the target year, announced shortly before 2022 began.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO because this was the executive budget priority he promoted.
contrary_evidence: Announcements do not prove implementation quality or economic payoff.
Strategic megaprojects may have large opportunity costs or weak returns.

evidence.claim: AMLO described direct school budgets, scholarships, pensions for older adults, disability support, and a planned 25 percent pension increase, all as part of his administration’s welfare system.
evidence.title: 12.10.22 Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador
evidence.publisher: Presidencia de la República 2018-2024 | Gobierno | gob.mx
evidence.excerpt: AMLO described direct school budgets, scholarships, pensions for older adults, disability support, and a planned 25 percent pension increase, all as part of his administration’s welfare system.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ruler speech documenting policy priorities and implementation details.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 ruler-period policy speech and program description.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Fully attributable to AMLO as his own official morning conference and stated policy agenda.
contrary_evidence: This is implementation rhetoric, not independent proof of final welfare outcomes.
The benefits may be offset by inflation and other macro pressures.

evidence.claim: Between the fourth quarter of 2021 and the fourth quarter of 2022, labor poverty fell from 40.3 percent to 38.5 percent, real labor income per capita rose 4.3 percent, and the number of employed people increased by 1.7 million, though labor poverty remained above pre-pandemic levels.
evidence.title: EL CONEVAL PRESENTA INFORMACIÓN REFERENTE A LA POBREZA LABORAL AL CUARTO TRIMESTRE DE 2022
evidence.excerpt: Between the fourth quarter of 2021 and the fourth quarter of 2022, labor poverty fell from 40.3 percent to 38.5 percent, real labor income per capita rose 4.3 percent, and the number of employed people increased by 1.7 million, though labor poverty remained above pre-pandemic levels.
evidence.source_locator: bullet summary and discussion around lines 153-180
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary national statistics source with precise 2022 household-labor measures.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the target year and closes the year with official 2022 labor-market evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to AMLO only in the sense that his wage and welfare policies were one input; the report itself also reflects external recovery and labor-market dynamics.
contrary_evidence: The report does not isolate AMLO policy from the broader recovery.
Labor poverty was still above pre-pandemic levels.

evidence.claim: Between 2018 and 2022, multidimensional poverty in Mexico fell from 41.9 percent to 36.3 percent, and the number of people in poverty fell from 51.9 million to 46.8 million.
evidence.title: Comunicado No. 7, El CONEVAL presenta las estimaciones de pobreza multidimensional 2022
evidence.excerpt: Between 2018 and 2022, multidimensional poverty in Mexico fell from 41.9 percent to 36.3 percent, and the number of people in poverty fell from 51.9 million to 46.8 million.
evidence.source_locator: page 0 and page 3 of the PDF, lines 13-19 and 136-147
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official poverty release with explicit national estimates and a clear target-year fit.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on the 2018-2022 period, directly covering the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to AMLO because it captures his full sexenio to 2022, but the report itself also reflects pandemic recovery and remittances.
contrary_evidence: The period starts in 2018, so part of the change predates some 2022 policy choices.
The report does not itself isolate the contribution of one president versus external conditions.

evidence.claim: AMLO’s plan to increase state control of electricity generation was defeated in Congress, with opponents warning it would hurt investment and breach international obligations.
evidence.title: Mexican president's contentious electricity overhaul defeated in Congress
evidence.excerpt: AMLO’s plan to increase state control of electricity generation was defeated in Congress, with opponents warning it would hurt investment and breach international obligations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a concrete legislative defeat with direct policy implications for investment and competition.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 policy conflict in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because it was AMLO’s plan and his governing coalition pushed it.
contrary_evidence: AMLO framed the overhaul as protecting public interest and energy sovereignty.
Congress defeated the constitutional version, so the final policy outcome was partly blocked rather than fully enacted.

unresolved_gaps: Federal command attribution is still thin for several state-level protest, journalist, and policing incidents.
Independent evidence that AMLO strengthened courts, the INE, INAI, or other checks is still weak compared with the evidence of media hostility and electoral-pressure attempts.
Direct personal-nexus evidence on self-enrichment, hidden ownership, or preferential benefit remains thin, and several items are still allegations or self-reports.
Independent audit-level evidence on on-time, on-budget delivery and the causal split between AMLO policy and external tailwinds is still incomplete.
